_comment: Position-management ruleset. Copy to ~/.cherrypick/config/manage.json and keep only what you change: the file is merged key by key over this default, and a key the default does not have is reported, not applied. Every rule carries `evidence`, the kind of evidence behind it, reported beside its verdict: mechanics (exchange or option mechanics, or arithmetic), tested (a published test or our own declared study supports it), contested (tests point against it, or are mixed), practice (practitioner doctrine, no test) or ours (our own rule, no test). Money is gross of fees.

credit._comment: A trade opened for a net credit. capture = share of the credit kept; stop fires when the loss reaches loss_multiple_of_credit x the credit; time_exit acts at the nearest short's DTE (a winner may roll, a loser closes).

by_shape._comment: A shape's own capture and evidence, in place of the rule's (a field left out is the rule's). Any shape manage names may be added, a ratio butterfly by its quantities ("1-3-2"); a shape it never names is reported. One short strike of these is nearly always in the money, so the tastylive strategy guide (2023) takes them off at 25%.

time_exit._comment: skip_if_entered_inside: a trade whose nearest short was opened dte days or fewer before its expiry (read off the order chain) skips this exit and is managed by its take profit, stop and the expiry close.

debit._comment: A trade opened for a net debit (spreads, long options, diagonals). stop at -loss_fraction, take profit at +gain_fraction; time_exit uses short_leg_dte when the trade carries shorts, long_only_dte otherwise.

by_shape._comment: A shape's own gain_fraction and evidence. A calendar trades only the time value between its expiries, so the strategy guide takes it off at 10-25% of the debit; a zebra starts with no time value and takes 25%.

max_gain_cap._comment: A diagonal (a PMCC among them) is worth about its width at the short's expiry, so gain_fraction of its debit can sit past anything it can make. Its target is the lesser of that and share of its modelled gain by the short's expiry (the long at its own IV). No outside test.

diagonal_width._comment: Review a two-leg diagonal (a PMCC or its put mirror) with little left to make at the short's expiry, on its net debit with rolls counted. Modelled with the long at its own IV: its best case under net / max_share_of_width (a third over the net at 75%), or the spread worth under the net run_past_short_moves expected moves past the short strike. A long expiring soon after the short peaks near the width, so that is the width rule; a long with years left keeps time value. No IV: the width rule itself.

price_stop._comment: A calendar's stop on the underlying's price: the band where its modelled value at the short's expiry (the long at its own IV) falls loss_share below the debit. Outside it the trade is reviewed, to close if the stock closes there. No outside test; the debit stop stays as the backstop.

time_exit._comment: A diagonal or calendar whose nearest short was sold short_term_short_days or fewer before its expiry (read off the order chain) runs on the long's clock instead: the time exit fires when the long it is sold against reaches time_spread_long_dte.
time_exit._skip_comment: skip_if_entered_inside: a trade whose clock leg was opened inside its own exit (a debit spread bought at short_leg_dte or fewer, a long option at long_only_dte or fewer) skips it.

legs._comment: A short leg that has given up `capture` of its premium is bought back with its wings, whatever the trade does.

long_vertical._comment: A butterfly's (broken-wing, broken-heart) long spread worth share_of_width of its width is sold, keeping the short spread.

diagonal_short._short_term_comment: A short sold week by week (debit.time_exit.short_term_short_days) is due at the expiry close or when captured, and rolls to the first quoted expiry at least short_term_out_days later (else the first monthly that far out), while the long outlives it by short_term_min_long_days.

fly_off._comment: A broken-wing butterfly opened for a credit: buy the wing that makes it a plain butterfly and sell the wide one, when that costs at most max_share_of_credit of the net credit. The new wing is modelled.

untested_side._comment: A short strangle or straddle with one short at tested_delta or more and the other under target_delta: roll the untested short toward the money, same expiry, to the listed strike nearest target_delta, for at least min_credit a share at the snapshot's quoted mids (roll_chains). A review; in place of the short-leg buy-back when that names the untested leg; never in place of a stop. Never past the tested strike: an inversion ranks below closing or rolling out in time, so it is only recorded, never proposed. Off by default since 2026-10-20; set enabled to true to use it.

wheel._comment: Rules on a wheel cycle's shorts and shares (the evaluation's wheel view). Only on a cycle that reconciles; an unreconciled one gets a review saying so and nothing else. They rank with every other rule by action: a close or stop outranks the wheel's roll.

take_profit._comment: Buy the short back when its mark is at or under the resting buy-to-close's price, else btc_price (btc_price_illiquid when its market is wide).

tested._comment: A short at or through its strike: roll or close. The net-zero and premium-gambit rolls out in time are priced on the snapshot's quoted chain and each judged by check-roll.

next_leg._comment: Shares an assignment delivered and not yet written against: name the covered call at the skate call band (band: fixed or by_expiry). No strike without the band.

covered_call._comment: Short calls the name's shares cover (100 a contract, all of them). The credit stop, breached close, oversize review and expiry close never judge them, since the shares cover each risk, and a losing call's time exit does not buy it back. An in-the-money call is judged by its call-away against the wheel basis (else the shares' own order chain cost, never the positions' open price): at or over it a review to let the shares go or roll up and out for a credit; under it roll or close; with no basis, a review saying so.

pmcc._comment: The PMCC view. A call diagonal (one long call, one short call of the same size at or above its strike expiring first, no shares; neither leg's days left decides it) is a PMCC only when its long was entered at entry_min_delta or more, or positions.<SYMBOL>.intent is "pmcc"; "diagonal" keeps it out. Its rules fire only on a recognised PMCC whose orders reconcile, rank with the diagonal rules by action, and give way to the diagonal's credit roll.

entry_record._comment: The long's delta at entry, recorded once from the first full snapshot after a call is bought (the underlying's price there, about 30-90 s after the fill), and preferred to the solve from the entry day's close. A fill whose snapshot came more than max_gap_seconds after it is not recorded and keeps the close. Each record carries the delta at a two-standard-deviation move over the gap, and a band across the floor is said in the recognition.

width._comment: Roll or close when the short strike less the long strike does not exceed the long's net cost per share after every premium collected: an assignment there locks in a loss. A net cost over warn_share of the width passes but is flagged thin (a call-away then earns under a third of the cost).

assignment._comment: Roll or close a short in the money with less time value than the next dividend before an ex-date inside its life, or under near_zero_extrinsic at any time.

roll_long._comment: Review rolling the long when it has days_left or fewer, or its delta is under min_delta.

roll._comment: The short's roll candidates: one per quoted expiry after the short and before the long, the next `expiries`, delta at most max_delta, a roll costing at most max_debit a share.

expiry._comment: Physically-settled legs are closed at or inside close_by_dte; roots listed as cash-settled settle instead. wait_if_entered_inside: legs all opened close_by_dte days or fewer before their expiry (read off the order chain) close on the expiry day, before its close, instead of at the first evaluation.

earnings_trade._comment: A trade put on to hold through an earnings report: opened min_days_before..max_days_before days before the call (0-7; the report's own day only for a call after the close), its nearest short expiring no more than max_days_expiry_after days after it. Until the call its close, take-profit and roll rules wait (shown as waiting), and so does the expiry close when the trade comes off after the call on or before its legs' expiry day (that morning, before the close it guards); the day after the report (the report's own day if before the open) it closes, unless it is losing with a leg in a later expiry (diagonal, calendar), which is left to the ordinary rules. Ex-dividend, sizing and unpriced-leg rules never wait, nor does expiry for a trade closing on its expiry day. Disable per name with positions.<SYM>.disable ["earnings_trade"].

attention._comment: Needs a look: a short option out of the money by near_pct of its strike or less, in the money, or likely to be exercised early (a call's time value under the dividend going ex before expiry, or any short's under near_zero_extrinsic); and every leg with expiring_days or fewer left. A reading, not a rule: it fires nothing. The orchestrator posts a name the first time it appears in a day.

early._comment: Marks taken between the open (09:30) and verdicts_from (New York) are the opening scramble: the evaluation is marked early, surfaces show prices, P&L and needs-a-look but hold the verdicts back, and the orchestrator does not post the list.

limits._comment: Your limits, each beside the book on Live -> portfolio. Blank (null) falls back to the guidance band where one exists (delta, theta, buying power) or the candidate cap (one name); dollar delta and vega have none. delta_bwd, dollar_delta and vega are +/-; theta_day a ceiling in dollars a day; buying_power_pct and per_name_pct shares of net liq. The day's loss posts once a session at day_loss_alert dollars, else day_loss_alert_pct of net liq. near_share: a row is near past this share of the way to its limit.

portfolio._comment: The account as one book: beta-weighted delta (in SPY shares, on the broker's beta), theta per calendar day, the break-even move and a stress line. Retail heuristics with no published out-of-sample evidence: practice, or ours where the figure is our own. Guidance is REVIEW, naming what drives it. enabled: false turns all of it off; the reading is still recorded.

theta._comment: Theta as a share of net liq per day. Above max the book sells more gamma than the band allows; under min only informs. The band, concentration and the candidates' theta cap leave out option legs front_dte days or less from expiry, whose theta is about to vanish; the raw figure is shown beside it.
theta._target_pct_nlv: The premium pace's target on the same figure: theta to hold inside the band, not to maximise.

delta._comment: BWD band: -short_per_theta x theta to +long_per_theta x theta SPY shares, on theta without the legs theta.front_dte days or less from expiry. Never narrower than, and with no positive theta equal to, +/- the BWD whose 1% move costs fallback_pct_nlv_per_1pct of net liq.

breakeven._comment: A short-gamma book whose break-even SPY move is under this multiple of SPY's implied one-day move.

concentration._comment: One underlying over max_share of the book's gross theta or gross beta-weighted delta. A position can be excused with positions.<SYM>.disable.

earnings_exposure._comment: What the trades with an earnings report before their nearest short expires can still lose, summed, over max_pct_nlv of net liq. Each trade passes its own rules; this adds them up.

expiry_concentration._comment: What the trades whose nearest short expires on one date can still lose, over max_pct_nlv of net liq. A new income candidate on an expiry already over it waits.

beta_doubt._comment: Flag a broker beta whose sign disagrees with its three-month correlation (|corr| >= min_abs_corr), or that is near zero beside a strong correlation.

stress._comment: SPY shocks the book is repriced at, each underlying moved by beta x shock, IV and time held still.

vol_expansion._comment: The book repriced at a vol expansion: SPY moved by move (each name by beta x move) with IVs up iv_shift vol points for a 30-day option, term-weighted as the risk matrix is, time held still. Over max_loss_pct_nlv of net liq is a REVIEW naming the names shortest vega. No published band exists: the shock and the cap are ours.

buying_power._comment: Buying power used against a ceiling. On margin it rises with VIX: [VIX under, cap] pairs, the last bound null for anything above; the common retail table, written for margin, where a short put holds a fraction of its notional and the hold grows as the stock falls. No VIX, no band. An account of unknown kind is judged here too.

cash._comment: A cash account or IRA holds each short put's full strike and each spread's max loss, and neither grows when the market moves, so its buying power is judged in parts instead of by VIX: max_pct_nlv in total (the rest kept free to sell after a vol spike); stock_exposure_pct_nlv for short puts at their strikes plus shares held (the stock the account owns or can be made to own); spread_risk_pct_nlv for the buying power everything else holds, its most it can lose. stress: SPY moved by move (each name by beta x move) with IVs up iv_shift (term-weighted), losing over max_loss_pct_nlv of net liq, is a REVIEW (portfolio.stress). The figures are ours, with no published evidence. enabled false judges a cash account by the VIX table.

scenarios._comment: The risk matrix (SPY moves x IV shifts in vol points for a 30-day option, time held still; with iv_shift_weighting "term" each leg's shift is scaled by sqrt(30 / DTE) so front months move most, "flat" shifts every leg alike) and the risk graph ([from, to, step] of SPY moves, now and at the nearest expiry).
scenarios._horizons: The matrix again at each of these many days on, nothing done meanwhile (legs expiring by then at intrinsic): with time held still it shows what the book risks and never the decay it is paid.

realistic._comment: A row with IV moved as VIX has moved when SPX moved this much: over windows of the horizon's trading days (never under min_window_days) since `since`, from the snapshot's Cboe closes, VIX's median end/start ratio among the windows whose SPX return was within `band` of the move's size (never under min_band). Fewer than min_windows such windows and the cell is blank. The shift is today's VIX x (ratio - 1) for a 30-day option, term-weighted like the other rows.

ideas._comment: Ideas for reshaping the book, under the risk matrix: each states what the change would do to the matrix's row now (the realistic row where there is one) and to theta. The thresholds are ours, with no published evidence; ideas inform and never size, place or close anything.

index_bucket._comment: Broad indexes that move together, and the share of net liq they may risk between them (each trade's modelled downside from now, summed).

trade_size._comment: One trade whose downside is over the candidates' per_trade_risk_pct of net liq.

short_dated_theta._comment: One trade paying over max_share of the book's theta from a short leg within_days or less from expiry: income that ends with the leg.

call_side._comment: Credit trades selling both sides whose short calls' IV is at most max_call_put_iv of their short puts': the cheap side sold for a like-sized loss (call spreads lost at every delta in the credit-spread studies, items 14-16).

expiry_cluster._comment: One expiry whose trades can lose over max_pct_nlv of net liq together: a planning target for spreading entries, tighter than the expiry_concentration review.

hedge._comment: When portfolio.delta fires, size an XSP vertical toward a target `inset` of the band's width inside the breached edge: a credit spread (short at credit_short_delta) and a debit spread (long at debit_long_delta), each `width` points wide, at most max_units. A credit spread never takes buying power used past max_buying_power_pct of net liq; a debit spread only lowers the worst case, so it is offered past the cap and flagged. Priced at mid, with the natural price beside it; nothing is placed.

collar._comment: A third kind, with no tested edge (research item 55): the debit spread plus a credit spread on the other side (too long: a put debit spread and a call credit spread; too short: the mirror), the credit short chosen so the net at mid is nearest zero. Offered only when that net is within max_net a share, credit or debit, and the short is at least min_short_delta out. Both halves are verticals, so no call is naked. It gives up the move past the short strike, and with put skew the call sits nearer the money than the put. Its worst case at expiry counts against max_buying_power_pct like a credit spread's.

delta_ideas._comment: The direction card's ideas: the drivers trades whose delta makes the book's, and the ways to move delta without closing anything, in both directions, on every evaluation. A time spread's short within front_days of expiry is rolled to the strike that moves delta most, its delta at most roll_short_delta; a credit trade selling both sides in one expiry rolls its untested side toward untested_short_delta, keeping its width and never past the other short; each for at least min_credit a share. new_spread adds one unit of the hedge's own credit and debit spreads. Priced at quoted mids; flags name the ruleset or sizing rule a roll goes against. Ours, no published evidence; nothing is placed.

candidates._comment: Income trades from our own universe (the evening income reading), sized to the account. Structures: a short put at short_put_delta; a put credit spread short the out-of-the-money strike nearest spread_short_delta, long nearest spread_long_delta beyond it, at least spread_min_credit of the width at the working price (0: no floor; the credit and the odds are shown), and a call spread the same way only with call_spreads on -- the least-bad cell of the 2026-10 credit-spread studies, none of which found an edge after costs, so every spread says no tested edge; a covered call at covered_call_delta on held shares only, on its own expiry (the monthly 30-45 days out, else the cycle monthly). The two deltas are the Screeners lists' 16 (2026-10-19); a short put or covered call whose nearest strike misses its delta by more than delta_tolerance is not built, as the lists drop it. Each gets the largest quantity that keeps one unit's stress loss (a spread's max loss) under per_trade_risk_pct of net liq, a short put's notional under notional_per_name_pct (by account kind), buying power under the VIX-scaled cap (else max_buying_power_pct), delta in its band, theta under its ceiling and the name under max_name_theta_share of the book's theta; the cap that stops it is named. Listed by symbol: with no tested edge, any ranking would read as one. One stopped only by how full the book is (buying power, the theta ceiling) is listed as waiting, sized as if there were room and graded by the buying power it would leave: under the cap ok, up to bp_warn_over above it over, beyond that far over. Modelled at mid from a day-old reading: re-quote before sending.

time_spreads._comment: The time-spread scanner's rows sized to the account: buying power after the trade at most max_bp_share of net liq, the candidates' per-trade risk and other caps otherwise, at most max_units. Above delta_limit beta-weighted delta only neutral and bearish structures are listed. No tested edge: rows are ordered by the front/back IV ratio, an untested hypothesis (item 54).

_positions_comment: Per-underlying overrides, e.g. {"SPY": {"intent": "hedge", "disable": ["debit.stop"], "note": "portfolio hedge"}}. intent "pmcc" recognises a call diagonal as a PMCC, "diagonal" keeps it out. Rule ids: expiry, credit.take_profit, credit.stop, credit.time_exit, credit.breached, credit.close_before_earnings, debit.stop, debit.take_profit, debit.diagonal_width, debit.price_stop, debit.time_exit, legs.short_take_profit, legs.long_vertical, roll.naked_put, roll.diagonal_short, roll.fly_off, roll.untested_side, wheel.take_profit, wheel.tested, wheel.next_leg, pmcc.width, pmcc.assignment, pmcc.roll_long, directional.take_profit, directional.stop, ex_dividend, risk.oversize, earnings_trade, portfolio.theta, portfolio.delta, portfolio.breakeven, portfolio.concentration, portfolio.buying_power, portfolio.stress, portfolio.earnings_exposure, portfolio.expiry_concentration, portfolio.vol_expansion
_trades_comment: Per-trade overrides, keyed two ways. By a trade's stable ID as the cards show it (e.g. XYZ-260401-1), for that trade alone, read over positions.<SYMBOL>: {"XYZ-260401-1": {"intent": "hedge", "disable": ["debit.stop"], "note": "..."}}; disable lists add up with the name's. By a PMCC's long contract as the broker spells it (spaces ignored), e.g. {"XYZ 280121C00040000": {"intent": "pmcc", "note": "bought as a PMCC"}}. intent "pmcc" or "diagonal" decides that PMCC alone and beats positions.<SYMBOL>.intent; the Live -> pmcc card shows the key. A rolled long is a new PMCC: the old contract's intent does not carry over. continues names the long this one replaced in a roll done in two orders, e.g. {"XYZ 280616C00040000": {"continues": "XYZ 280121C00040000"}}, so the old long's cash and the shorts sold against it stay in the chain (a roll in one order links on its own); the card flags a possible two-order roll and gives the line to add.
